In physics, the university was the site of the Chicago Pile-1 (the first self-sustained man-made nuclear reaction, part of the Manhattan Project), of Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment that calculated the charge of the electron, and of the development of radiocarbon dating by Willard F. REM sleep was discovered at the university in 1953 by Nathaniel Kleitman and Eugene Aserinsky.
